messages:
Priya (AE): Quick question — Acme Payments wants to run a short POC: streaming via their WASM edge adapter, multiplex many logical streams over one connection, per-stream QoS/priority, and structured function-call outputs. Any red flags or known limits?
Jordan (SE): Sounds achievable. Two quick asks: are they planning to use SSE or a websocket proxy? And which WASM runtime — Wasmtime/wasmEdge?
Priya (AE): They said Wasmtime inside a worker pool + websocket multiplexing (custom). Also they want per-customer rate limits and priority queues (gold/silver). Concerned about cost when lots of small bursts.
Tom (SDK): Multiplexing is fine but changes batching behavior. Fewer TCP connections reduces overhead, but the server-side runtime needs per-stream metadata to manage KV cache. Recommend adding a custom header like `x-rw-stream-id` and `x-rw-priority`. Example minimal proxy snippet: ```
# proxy -> redwood
GET /stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.com
Upgrade: websocket
x-rw-stream-id: <uuid>
x-rw-priority: gold

# client sends frames tagged with stream-id, server routes into separate gen sessions
```
Jordan (SE): For QoS, use a router policy that sets token budget per-priority and `max_inflight_per_stream`. Fallback: route to quantized model variant when latency SLOs would be violated. Config knobs: `route_policy: latency_priority`, `fallback_model: gpt-q4f16`, `max_inflight_per_stream: 4`.
Elena (Security): Security checklist: if adapter runs in customer infra, require mTLS between adapter and our ingestion endpoint, IP allowlist, and short-lived creds for token exchange. For on-prem connector we need KMS integration and audit logs. If they want SOC2 answers, I can attach the standard pack.
Priya (AE): Pricing ask: can we rough-estimate cost for 1k concurrent streams, average 40 tokens/sec per stream, run for 8 hours? They want a ballpark to see if Dedicated is worth it.
Tom (SDK): BOE calc: tokens/sec = 40, per stream over 8h = 40 * 3600 * 8 = 1,152,000 tokens/stream. For 1k streams => 1.152e9 tokens. At hosted rate $0.00003/token => ~$34,560. If you use a cheaper quantized model at $0.000008/token => ~$9,216. Note this ignores batching gains and caching — multiplexing + batching may lower effective tokens billed if you use prefix caching and shorter context windows.
Jordan (SE): Also highlight Dedicated/reserved capacity: with a commitment we can guarantee throughput and likely lower unit price — and easier to hit QoS SLAs. For a POC, suggest starting hosted in a dedicated sandbox to validate integration, then move to Dedicated if latency/cost requires.
Priya (AE): Action items: (1) share WASM adapter example repo with Acme (Tom), (2) produce a formal quote with hosted vs dedicated numbers (Jordan + Finance), (3) security questionnaire answers & pack (Elena). I'll open a POC ticket and schedule kickoff.
Elena (Security): I'll draft the SQA answers and include KMS/SOC2 snippets. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Tom (SDK): Pushed sample repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/tree/main/wasm/stream-proxy — includes stream-id header example and small go runtime helper. Also small test harness:```bash
# run local adapter test
go run ./examples/wasm/stream-proxy/testclient --endpoint ws://staging.api.redwood.com/stream --streams 10 --rate 40
```
Jordan (SE): I'll prep the Dedicated capacity estimate and a slide with routing policy examples. Can join the kickoff tomorrow 9am PT.
deploy-bot: example/wasm/stream-proxy v0.7 deployed to staging in us-west-2 :rocket:
Priya (AE): Thanks team. @Jordan pls confirm meeting time with Acme. I'll start the POC ticket and attach this thread and the security checklist.
Jordan (SE): Confirmed — pinged Acme. Meeting set for tomorrow 9am PT.
Priya (AE): Perfect, closing loop for now.
